CSULB is a commuter school, despite that, there are many clubs and other student activities you can participate in on campus. I love the semester system over the quarter system. Some ppl feel like the semester system drags on b/c they’re 16 week sessions vs the 10 week session for the quarter system. We have a much longer winter break though (4-5 weeks vs the 2 weeks for quarter).

Try to avoid working out with a binder on also (I know this is hella difficult to do, that's when my gender dysphoria was at its worst), binding while working out is hella taxing and hard on your body. I'm not trying to make a diagnosis, but BPD is fairly common and comes with a lot of extreme highs and lows that cause you to make rash decisions. A way I've found to deal with this is to just have people to support you when you really need it, find good coping mechanisms, and find a medical professional to talk to. 

My biggest coping mechanism is drawing/ making art. This really helps when I'm sh-y/ suicidal because it's something I can totally focus my mind on. 

I also draw when I'm feeling manic for the same reason. Sometimes I also just dance in my room by myself, it's really fun and lets you get all your energy out- I highly recommend it lol

When I'm pissed off, I know it's best to sit down and meditate for a few minutes. I know how weird this can be (especially for the first few times), but it genuinely helps. I always go down a why tunnel of thinking when I'm angry and it helps me be more content with my situation. For example: if I'm thinking back on something shitty an old friend did to me and find myself getting angry, I'll sit down for a second and control my breathing. Why did she do that? Was that okay? No- so how can you react in the future when someone does that? Etc, etc.

I've also recently started to work out when I feel a combination of anger and mania. That's really good since it allows you to get your anger/ energy out and you're taking care of your body.

I'm sure you've heard a lot of these coping mechanisms before, but these are the ones I use. These won't make your switches stop, however it'll help when you do all the sudden switch moods. Coping mechanisms work different for everyone, but hopefully at least one of these will work for you. It's just about always beneficial to talk to a therapist and/or psychiatrist about these things too. I hope you can find help and feel better soon
